headline: DeepSeek Opens Its Inference Engine
lede: DeepInfer is now Apache 2.0, exposing the machinery behind DeepSeek’s production serving stack. It brings distributed parallelism, speculative decoding, and deterministic sampling into the open—though the surrounding service architecture remains yours to build.

headline: A Monospace Font Built for Adventure
lede: Nordwand Mono began as a Python-built type project and became a configurable coding font with multiple weights, Cyrillic support, and optional ligatures. Its source lets terminal dwellers tune the furniture of their own workspace.

headline: OpenBSD 8.0 Extends the Secure Base
lede: OpenBSD’s 61st release adds hardware support, larger virtual machines, and refinements across networking and drivers. Beneath the release notes sits the familiar project discipline: portability, correctness, and hardening first.

headline: microG Rebuilds Android’s Missing Middle
lede: microG recreates the proprietary Google Mobile Services layer as free software, giving custom Android systems compatible APIs without Google’s closed framework. It is infrastructure for devices that want Android’s applications without surrendering the whole platform.

headline: WhatsApp’s Hidden Instructions Steer Users Away
lede: Machine-readable notes in WhatsApp help pages told a support bot not to recommend regulators or cite privacy laws in some disputes. The instructions were removed after disclosure, but the episode leaves a blunt question: whose rights does the assistant explain?

headline: 421,179 Emails Expose AfD’s Inner World
lede: A hacked archive of 421,179 messages offers a vast, troubling record of conversations inside Germany’s far-right party. AI-generated summaries make the trove searchable, but authenticity, context, and the ethics of publishing private correspondence remain central.

headline: Blocking Prox1 Restores Retinal Regeneration
lede: In injured mice, reducing the transfer of Prox1 into Müller glia allowed those cells to produce new retinal neurons. An antibody-fragment gene therapy showed related effects in a retinitis pigmentosa model, an intriguing preclinical result rather than a human treatment.

headline: When ESG Screening Blocks Defence Startups
lede: UK defence startups reportedly face bank-account refusals when compliance systems treat their work as an undifferentiated reputational risk. The dispute exposes a widening gap between political support for defence investment and the quiet decisions made by financial gatekeepers.
pullquote: A compliance category can become an industrial policy without anyone announcing it.

headline: U.S. Agencies Ordered Away from DeepSeek
lede: A new DHS order reportedly bars DeepSeek services from U.S. federal civilian systems. The practical boundary is still being parsed—especially for locally hosted models—but procurement, data handling, and supply-chain risk are now part of the same warning label.

headline: XScreenSaver Has No Official GitHub
lede: Jamie Zawinski’s project distributes official XScreenSaver releases as website-hosted tar files, not through a public GitHub repository. Treat the many mirrors as artifacts of the surrounding ecosystem, not as proof of provenance.
